held_because: 3 confirmed findings (subject of ephesen, tense of gnorisai, bracketed pepoiekenai); sentence re-translated from the Greek (Claude, 2026-10-15)
source:
Ὥσπερ γὰρ ὅλου τοῦ σώματος ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐνεργουμένου, καὶ φωτιζομένου, εἴ τις λέγοι ἄτοπον εἶναι καὶ ἐν τῷ δακτύλῳ τοῦ ποδὸς τὴν δύναμιν εἶναι τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀνόητος ἂν νομισθείη, ὅτι διδοὺς ἐν τῷ ὅλῳ αὐτὸν διικνεῖσθαι καὶ ἐνεργεῖν, κωλύει καὶ ἐν τῷ μέρει αὐτὸν εἶναι· οὕτως ὁ διδοὺς καὶ πιστεύων τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγον ἐν τῷ παντὶ εἶναι, καὶ τὸ πᾶν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ φωτίζεσθαι καὶ κινεῖσθαι, οὐκ ἄτοπον ἂν ἡγήσηται, καὶ σῶμα ἓν ἀνθρώπινον ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ κινεῖσθαι καὶ φωτίζεσθαι.
Εἰ δὲ ὅτι γενητόν ἐστι, καὶ ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων γέγονε τὸ ἀνθρώπινον γένος διᾶ τοῦτο οὐκ εὐπρεπῆ νομίζουσιν ἡμᾶς λέγειν τὴν ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἐπιφάνειαν· ὥρα καὶ τῆς κτίσεως αὐτοὺς αὐτὸν ἐκβάλλειν· καὶ γὰρ καὶ αὕτη ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος εἰς τὸ εἶναι διὰ τοῦ Λόγου γέγονεν.
Εἰ δὲ καὶ γενητῆς οὔσης τῆς κτίσεως, οὐκ ἄτοπον ἐν αὐτῇ τὸν Λόγον εἶναι, οὐκ ἄρα οὐδὲ ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ αὐτὸν εἶναι ἄτοπον. ὁποῖα γὰρ ἂν περὶ τοῦ ὅλου νοήσειαν, τοιαῦτα ἀνάγκη καὶ περὶ τοῦ μέρους αὐτοὺς ἐνθυμεῖσθαι. μέρος γὰρ, ὡς προεῖπον, τοῦ ὅλου καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπός ἐστιν.
Οὐκοῦν ὅλως οὐκ ἀπρεπὲς τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ εἶναι τὸν Λόγον, καὶ πάντα ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ φωτίζεσθαι, καὶ κινεῖσθαι, καὶ ἦν, καθὼς καὶ οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῖς συγγραφεῖς φασιν· ὅτι ἐν αὐτῇ ζῶμεν, καὶ κινούμεθα, καὶ ἐσμέν.
Τί λοιπὸν χλεύης ἄξιον λέγομεν, εἰ ἐν ᾧ ἔστιν ὁ Λόγος, τούτῳ πρὸς φανέρωσιν ὡς ὀργάνῳ κέχρηται ὁ Λόγος; εἰ μὲν γὰρ οὐκ ἦν ἐν αὐτῷ, οὐδὲ χρήσασθαι ἂν ἠδυνήθη τούτῳ. εἰ δὲ προαποδεδώκαμεν ἐν τῷ παντὶ καὶ ἐν τοῖς κατὰ μέρος εἶναι τοῦτον, τί ἄπιστον εἰ ἐν οἷς ἔστιν ἐν τούτοις ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἐπιφαίνει;
Ὥσπερ γὰρ ταῖς ἑαυτοῦ δυνάμεσιν ὅλος ἐν ἑκάστῳ καὶ πᾶσιν ἐπιβαίνων, καὶ πάντα διακοσμῶν ἀφθόνως, εἰ ἤθελε, διὰ ἡλίου, ἢ σελήνης, ἢ οὐρανοῦ, ἢ γῆς, ἢ ὑδάτων, ἢ πυρός, οὐκ ἄν τις ἀτόπως αὐτὸν? φωνῇ χρήσασθαι καὶ γνωρίσαι ἑαυτὸν καὶ τὸν αὐτοῦ Πατέρα ἔφησεν [πεποιηκέναι] ἅπαξ πάντα αὐτοῦ συνέχοντος καὶ μετὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ μέρει τυγχάνοντος καὶ ἀοράτως ἑαυτὸν δεικνύντος· οὕτως οὐκ ἄτοπον ἂν εἴη διακοσμοῦντα αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα καὶ τὰ ὅλα ζωοποιοῦντα, καὶ θελήσαντα δι’ ἀνθρώπων γνωρίσαι, εἰ ὀργάνῳ κέχρηται ἀνθρώπου σώματι πρὸς φανέρωσιν ἀληθείας καὶ γνῶσιν τοῦ Πατρός. μέρος γὰρ τοῦ ὅλου καὶ ἡ ἀνθρωπότης τυγχάνει.
Καὶ ὥσπερ ὁ νοῦς δι’ ὅλου τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὤν, ἀπὸ μέρους τοῦ σώματος, τῆς γλώττης λέγω, σημαίνεται, καὶ οὐ δήπου τις ἐλαττοῦσθαι τὴν οὐσίαν τοῦ νοῦ διὰ τοῦτο λέγει· οὕτως ὁ Λόγος διὰ πάντων ὤν, εἰ ἀνθρωπίνῳ κέχρηται ὀργάνῳ, οὐκ ἀπρεπὲς ἂν φαίνοιτο τοῦτο. εἰ γὰρ, ὡς προεῖπον, ἀπρεπὲς ὀργάνῳ χρήσασθαι σώματι, ἀπρεπὲς καὶ ἐν τῷ ὅλῳ αὐτὸν εἶναι.
english: Just as, when a man activates and illuminates his whole body, someone who said it was absurd for the man's power to be in the toe of his foot would be thought foolish, because in granting that the man extends through the whole and acts in it, he prevents him from being in the part—so the person who grants and believes that the Word of God is in the universe, and that the universe is illuminated and moved by him, should not think it absurd that one human body is also moved and illuminated by him.

But if they think it is unseemly for us to speak of the Savior's manifestation in a human being because the human race is generated and came into being from nothing, then it is time for them to cast him out of creation as well; for creation also came into being from nothing through the Word.

And if, even though creation is generated, it is not absurd for the Word to be in it, then it is not absurd for him to be in a human being either. For whatever they think about the whole, they must necessarily think about the part as well. For the human being, as I said before, is also a part of the whole.

Therefore it is not at all unseemly for the Word to be in a human being, and for all things to be illuminated and moved by him and in him—as even their own writers say: 'In him we live and move and have our being'.

What then do we say that deserves mockery, if the Word uses as an instrument for manifestation that in which he already is? For if he were not in it, he could not have used it. But if we have already granted that he is in the whole and in the parts, what is unbelievable if he also manifests himself in the things in which he is?

Just as, by his own powers he enters wholly into each and all things and orders all things ungrudgingly, if he had willed, through sun or moon or heaven or earth or waters or fire, he would have declared by a voice that he had made himself and his Father known, since he holds all things together at once, and is present with all things and in the part itself, showing himself invisibly—so it would not be absurd for him, who orders all things and gives life to the whole, to have willed to make himself known through human beings, if he used a human body as an instrument for the manifestation of truth and the knowledge of the Father. For humanity also is a part of the whole.

And just as the mind, being throughout the whole man, is signified by a part of the body—I mean the tongue—and no one surely says that the substance of the mind is diminished because of this, so the Word, being through all things, would not appear unseemly if he used a human instrument. For if, as I said before, it is unseemly to use a body as an instrument, it is unseemly also for him to be in the whole.

findings.quote: he would have declared by a voice that he had made himself and his Father known
findings.checker_says: Subject confusion: 'he would have declared' makes God the subject of ἔφησεν, but the Greek says 'one would not absurdly say that he used a voice and made known...'

findings.quote: he had made himself and his Father known
findings.checker_says: Tense error: γνωρίσαι is aorist infinitive 'to make known,' not pluperfect 'had made known'; this is about potential action, not completed past

findings.quote: he had made himself and his Father known
findings.checker_says: Bracketed [πεποιηκέναι] is a scribal gloss; translating it as 'had made' adds uncertain text as definite
